newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Five reported killed in Nigerian Moslem clashes.
newsitem.headline: Five reported killed in Nigerian Moslem clashes.

text.p: Three Moslems and two policemen were killed in the northern Nigerian city of Kaduna on Wednesday when Shi'ite Moslems clashed with police, a Moslem group said.

A police spokeswoman told Reuters by telephone from Kaduna that two policemen were killed, but said she had no information on reports that three Moslems had been shot dead by riot police in Kaduna central market.
The clashes came after demonstrations by Shi'ite Moslems in Kaduna against the detention of their leaders. At the demonstrations police fired teargas to disperse the protesters.
"The police shot three of our people dead at the central market where two of their men were lynched by the mob," a member of the Shi'ite Moslem Brotherhood said.

Police in the mainly Moslem north, scene of bloody religious riots in the past, have been on alert over an ultimatum given by the Shi'ite group after its leader Ibrahim Yakub El-Zak-Zaky and others were arrested what police called for security reasons.
On Saturday the Shi'ites Moslem Brotherhood said 14 people had been killed in clashes with police at the weekend following El-Zak-Zaky's arrest but police deny there were deaths.
